record.paper_title: Mapping Class Group Factorizations and Symplectic 4-Manifolds: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: View a Lefschetz fibration with genus-g fibers as a smooth map phi from S^2 to the compactified moduli space of genus-g curves, where singular fibers correspond to positive transverse intersections with the divisor of nodal curves. Can one find special geometric representatives for such maps, for example trees of conformal harmonic maps, and use those representatives to decompose or understand Lefschetz fibrations in terms of holomorphic pieces?

artifact.category_tag: Lefschetz fibrations and moduli of curves
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ denote the Deligne–Mumford compactification of the moduli space of smooth complex projective curves of genus $g \ge 2$, and let $\Delta \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ be the boundary divisor parametrizing nodal curves. A genus-$g$ Lefschetz fibration $f : X 	o S^2$ on a smooth closed oriented 4-manifold $X$ (a smooth surjection whose critical points are modeled in local complex coordinates by $(z_1,z_2) \mapsto z_1^2+z_2^2$, with regular fibers diffeomorphic to a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface) determines a continuous classifying map
$$\varphi_f : S^2 \longrightarrow \overline{\mathcal{M}}_g,$$
well-defined up to homotopy, sending each regular value to the isomorphism class of its fiber and each critical value to the corresponding nodal curve, and meeting $\Delta$ positively and transversely at the critical values.

Question. Within the homotopy class of $\varphi_f$, does there exist a distinguished geometric representative built from holomorphic data — for example, a tree-like configuration of conformal harmonic maps from nodal Riemann surfaces (a "tree of conformal harmonic maps") into $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ representing $\varphi_f$ — such that this representative decomposes the Lefschetz fibration $f$ into holomorphic pieces (pieces over which the fibration is, up to deformation, the restriction of a holomorphic family of curves)?

In precise form: characterize the homotopy classes of maps $S^2 	o \overline{\mathcal{M}}_g$ that arise from Lefschetz fibrations, and determine whether every such class admits a canonical representative as a stable map / tree of conformal harmonic maps whose components correspond to maximal holomorphic sub-fibrations of $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, posed as a speculative direction relating Lefschetz fibrations to classifying maps into the Deligne–Mumford moduli space, appears to remain open. Related developments — such as the use of these classifying maps as symplectic invariants and recent work on achiral Lefschetz fibrations and moduli of curves — have appeared, but no construction of canonical "tree of conformal harmonic maps" representatives decomposing Lefschetz fibrations into holomorphic pieces has been established.

status_evidence.title: Lefschetz pencils and divisors in moduli space
status_evidence.snippet: Lefschetz pencils define maps from S^2 to the compactified moduli space of curves; for g large the isotopy class is a symplectic invariant.
status_evidence.claim: The viewpoint of Lefschetz fibrations as maps to moduli space is established, but the question of canonical geometric representatives remains a research direction.

status_evidence.title: Achiral Lefschetz fibrations and the moduli space of curves
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of classifying maps for achiral Lefschetz fibrations proven via Riemannian geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work extends the classifying-map perspective but does not produce canonical holomorphic/harmonic representatives decomposing Lefschetz fibrations.
